title: Death Cannot Make Our Souls Afraid
description: Death Cannot Make Our Souls Afraid in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 49, headed “Moses dying in the embraces of God”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Death can-not make our souls af-raid If God be with us there; We may walk thro' her dark-est shade, And nev-er yield to fear.

lines: Death cannot make our souls afraid
If God be with us there;
We may walk thro' her darkest shade,
I could renounce my all below,
And run, if I were call'd to go,
Might I but climb to Pisgah's top,
My flesh itself shall long to drop,
Clasp'd in my heavenly Father's arms
And lose my life among the charms

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
